desks.Dividends: MSFT goes ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98, the raised quarterly rate declared Sep 15 (+7.7%, its 24th consecutive annual increase) — the only declared watchlist ex-date in the next four weeks. AAPL's November dividend is still undeclared; the forecast ex-date of ~Nov 9 at the unchanged $0.27 rests on pattern only, and the declaration expected alongside late-October earnings is what would turn it into fact. SPY, QQQ, and NVDA next go ex in December, outside the window; TSLA pays no dividend. No cuts or specials announced.
desks.Earnings: MSFT Wed Oct 28 after close is the week's binary event: the Oct 30 straddle implies ~5.3% (mid $27.68 against $524.51). AAPL Mon Nov 2 after close follows: the Nov 6 straddle implies ~4.9% (mid $16.85 against $347.73). Both figures are straddle proxies spanning sessions beyond the event, not pure earnings-move isolates, and historical average earnings-day moves for both names are UNVERIFIED — no series was pulled. TSLA already reported Oct 21 and is priced in; NVDA (expected Nov 18) sits outside the window. The Nasdaq earnings-calendar API returned empty rows on this pull, so dates rest on company and press sources.
desks.Futures: Crude is pricing a geopolitical risk premium, not a confirmed supply shortfall. Brent settled Fri Oct 23 at $116.72 (+3.14% on the day, highest close since Apr 29) and WTI at $103.27 (+3.8%), a $13.45 spread, even as Middle East crude flows through Hormuz and alternative routes averaged above 24M barrels per day in the week through Oct 18, above the pre-war 23.3M. The EIA print argues against chasing the crude headline: crude drew 3.1M barrels and gasoline 3.0M, but distillates built 1.7M and Cushing built 0.9M. Natural gas storage rose 77 Bcf to 3,644 Bcf, near normal nationally with a South Central deficit. Grains run the other way: October WASDE raised corn to a near-record crop and pushed futures down ~5%. Next catalysts: EIA Wed Oct 28, EIA gas Thu Oct 29, WASDE Tue Nov 10.
desks.Parity: No new put-call or box parity violation found, and deterministic parity stands as the pricing constraint. The one methodology item: S&P Dow Jones Indices revises its growth/value style scoring — momentum drops from growth scoring, value scoring moves to an intangibles-adjusted book-to-price with earnings- and cash-flow-to-price blends — effective before market open Dec 21, 2026, with pro-forma files due Dec 4. That is a style-subindex reclassification, not a headline index membership change, so the direct effect on SPY/QQQ tracking is limited; the flow to watch is style-index fund rebalancing around Dec 21.
desks.Premium: Term structure slopes up everywhere because the earnings humps sit in the Nov 20 expiry, which contains MSFT (Oct 28), AAPL (Nov 2), and NVDA (Nov 18) — elevated back-month implied volatility for those names is expected event pricing, not rich premium. MSFT: 33.9% in Nov 20 against 18.5% front. No clean IV-versus-realized verdict for QQQ or AAPL: their realized windows are window-contingent (30.7% and 35.3% single-day shares), and NVDA at 29.9% is one large day from joining them. MSFT's window rolled clean (19.1%, versus 35.1% on the prior window) — a window change, not a contradiction. TSLA front IV (29.7%) sits below trailing 20-day realized (37.3%) on a clean window, backward-looking only. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names; no free IV-history source was available. Friday-close marks are not executable quotes, so no parity verdict is claimed from this pull.
desks.Quant lab: Seven candidates scored and appended to the ledger (#140-146): six ARCHIVE, one WATCH. The WATCH item is Keller-Ressel and Nikulski on discovering implied-volatility parametrizations with symbolic regression (arXiv:2603.21892): PySR conditional regression rediscovers SVI at complexity 15 under a Lee-tail wing-arbitrage penalty, with SVI-plus-one-term extensions fitting W-shaped curves. A secondary summary claiming a complexity-10 formula beat SVI is not what the paper shows — the complexity-10 penalized expression carries a larger loss than SVI-at-15. No author code link appears in the paper, so reproducibility is not established, though PySR itself is open source. Nothing reached TEST or INTEGRATE.

items.detail: Brent settled Fri Oct 23 at $116.72, up 3.14% on the day and its highest close since Apr 29, with WTI at $103.27 (+3.8%) — while Middle East crude flows through Hormuz and alternative routes averaged above 24M barrels per day in the week through Oct 18, above the pre-war 23.3M barrels per day. Saudi production was reported unaffected, though refined-product shipments were restricted. The price rise alongside recovered headline flows points to a fear and insurance premium — shipping risk and record Persian Gulf freight rates — rather than barrels already lost. The premium can unwind as fast as it built: escalation and de-escalation headlines both moved prices this week. The EIA print tempers the bull case further: crude and gasoline drew, but distillates built 1.7M barrels and Cushing built 0.9M.
items.title: Crude at $116 prices war premium, not lost barrels

items.detail: The latest FRED daily prints are dated Thu Oct 22 — Friday data had not landed at pull time, so these repeat yesterday's levels, a data lag rather than a new observation. The 2-year fell 16 basis points to 4.65% and the 10-year fell 17 to 4.96% on Oct 22, with the 2s10s spread at 31 basis points, still upward-sloping but 16 basis points flatter than 60 days ago. The fed funds effective rate is 3.88% and SOFR prints 3.90%, a 2-basis-point spread that signals no funding stress. One day of relief does not reverse a 60-day rise of 32 to 48 basis points: absolute levels near 5% on the 10-year remain a discount-rate headwind for long-duration names. The event stack into next week is the Oct 28 FOMC decision, with core PCE landing Oct 29, after the decision.
items.title: Rates eased sharply Oct 22 but stay high into the FOMC
